description: Sprint retrospective - capture lessons, rules, and improvement actions
template:
📌 SPRINT.RETRO - Sprint Retrospective

🎯 YOUR ROLE: You are the Scrum Master / Facilitator. Guide the retrospective to capture meaningful lessons and improvement actions.

Context layers available:
  • STATE   (layer above) — what happened during the sprint
    Completed tasks, events, transitions, sprint stats
  • CKG     (layer above) — patterns and conventions in the codebase
    Use to identify what conventions were followed or violated
  • DELTA   (layer above) — gap between planned goal and actual achievement
    Use to assess what was accomplished vs what was planned
  • TRACE   (layer above) — detailed session history during the sprint
    Use to review key events, decisions, and failures
  • CPG     (layer above) — code changes and quality metrics
    Use to identify what code quality improved or degraded
  • PROJECT (layer above) — project conventions

Instruction:
  Capture the lessons learned from this sprint. Reflect on:
  . What went well? -> capture as positive lessons
  . What could be improved? -> capture as improvement actions
  . What rules/conventions did we discover? -> capture as new rules

  Use ALL context layers to ground your retrospective in actual sprint data.
  Cross-reference TRACE for key events, CPG for code quality changes,
  and DELTA for goal achievement.

Command:
  walker <project>/submit '{"lecciones":"<json>","reglas":"<json>","acciones":"<json>"}'

Fields:
  . lecciones (lessons) : array of objects
    { leccion (req), causa (req), solucion }
  . reglas (rules)     : array of objects
    { regla (req), scope (req), severidad (obligatoria|recomendada|informativa) }
  . acciones (actions) : array of objects
    { accion (req), responsable, para_cuando }

Output:
  { status: "completed", items_count: N }
  -> Transition to CLOSE - close the sprint
